name: Vagabond / homeless maxxing

lead: Vagabond or homeless maxxing is a looksmaxxing-forum concept about adopting a drifter lifestyle. A thread on looksmax.org titled as an ultimate guide presents it with a sardonic, exaggerated tone, arguing from a rejection of conventional jobs and modern life.
The proposed appearance payoff is a rugged, unbound persona. The vagabond, an itinerant wanderer, is a long-standing figure in history, from medieval Europe through the hobo era in America.

paras: In the concept as discussed, it centres on low-cost mobility and quitting conventional routines. Versions framed around fitness describe outdoor movement and training while travelling.
Public-health sources document serious risks for people without stable housing: skin conditions such as scabies and body lice, infections, hypothermia and elevated mortality.

lead: Vagabond or homeless maxxing is a concept discussed on looksmaxxing forums about adopting a wandering, low-cost lifestyle as a route to a distinctive look and persona. The main discussion is a looksmax.org thread presenting an exaggerated guide; its tone is largely humorous.

A vagabond is an itinerant person who roams without fixed residence or steady employment; the word comes from Late Latin vagabundus and entered English via Old French in the 14th century.[1] Historical vagabondage followed events such as the Black Death and English enclosures, and later the hobo culture of rail-riding workers in the US.[1]
infobox: No studies of the looksmaxxing concept

paras: Vagabond lifestyles are distinguished from nomadism, which is tied to cultural or seasonal patterns, and from hobo travel, which historically centred on work-seeking by freight train.[1]

Public-health literature documents body-lice infestation ("vagabond's disease"), with a case report of lethal hypothermia worsened by lice-induced anaemia in an elderly man.[2] Homelessness is also associated with scabies, tuberculosis, chronic disease and sharply higher death rates.[3]
